briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. I will now begin the climate change expert spokesperson briefing for September 17, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 The Reality of Climate Catastrophe and International Warnings
sections.content: According to news reported today, Nepal experienced deadly glacial and rock collapses and massive floods, resulting in over 1,300 deaths. Scientists have analyzed that climate change increased the likelihood of such catastrophic events [5, 47, 50, 53, 68, 69, 70, 73, 74, 83, 84, 89, 94]. In this regard, there is growing international discussion that polluters should bear the costs if climate change contributed to the floods, alongside increasing calls for 'loss and damage' compensation for Nepal [51, 82]. Furthermore, in Bangladesh, dangerous heatwave days increased by 25 days during summer due to climate change, and Europe also experienced heatwaves and wildfires during the summer, indicating a global spread of extreme weather phenomena [77, 92]. This reality of the climate crisis once again underscores the need for immediate and robust action [61, 79].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Carbon Neutrality Efforts and Institutional Challenges
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts are underway to achieve carbon neutrality. The Climate Change Foundation is refining regional carbon neutrality targets using greenhouse gas data [2], and various local governments, including Gangnam-gu and Yangju-si, are hosting carbon neutrality camps and experiential festivals for citizens and future generations, encouraging daily practices [12, 15, 16, 17, 18, 27, 28]. The Korea Institute of Building Performance is exploring carbon neutrality solutions through a paradigm shift in urban regeneration projects, and Cheonan City and Hoseo University are actively engaging in public-private partnerships and community participation, including launching climate crisis response campaigns such as the Nepal flood solidarity campaign [11, 25, 29, 30]. However, due to institutional shortcomings, such as unpaid carbon neutrality points totaling 5.2 billion KRW over the past five years, citizens' efforts are not being adequately rewarded. This has made securing policy credibility an urgent task [7, 8, 9, 14, 20].

sections.title: 🌱 Acceleration of Renewable Energy Transition and Current Challenges
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating globally, and the Director-General of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA) expressed confidence that renewable energy is more competitive than nuclear power in meeting the increasing electricity demand from the AI and semiconductor industries [31, 33, 35]. Indeed, over the past five months, 4.4 trillion KRW in fossil fuel electricity purchase costs have been saved through renewable energy [45], and Spain is investing over 17 billion Euros in its power grid to meet renewable energy and data center demands, actively expanding its infrastructure [34]. Domestically, companies are notably increasing their efforts to procure renewable energy, with Naver investing in solar power and signing an MOU for solar power supply cooperation totaling 216MW [41, 43]. However, concerns about insufficient grid preparedness for increased solar power generation [4] and the potential collapse of the solar manufacturing base [36] suggest an urgent need for domestic policy support and infrastructure improvements to expand renewable energy. Furthermore, Greenpeace warned that despite achieving renewable energy procurement targets, fossil fuel power generation could increase in mega-projects, highlighting the difficulties in achieving carbon neutrality goals [6].

sections.title: 🌍 Global Cooperation and Policy Responses
sections.content: International cooperation and policy discussions to address climate change are steadily progressing. The 9th Korea-U.S. Joint Committee on Science and Technology agreed to implement climate change cooperation, signaling a reprioritization of policies [1], and the Speaker of the Mongolian Parliament urged stronger international cooperation to combat climate change [3]. The European Union (EU) is preparing to launch a climate insurance scheme following a summer of extreme weather [48], and India is pursuing digital transformation to combat climate change, launching a net-zero and action plan platform [88]. Meanwhile, an analysis suggesting that a reduction in the amount of dust in Earth's atmosphere could contribute to global warming has also been raised, emphasizing the importance of new scientific understanding [59]. Telford and Wrekin Council has achieved concrete results, successfully reducing carbon emissions by 69% on its journey towards carbon neutrality [93], and a positive outlook also emerged, forecasting a global reduction of approximately 0.5% in fossil fuel emissions in 2026 [96].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the reality of the climate crisis and the diverse domestic and international efforts to address it. Through continuous international cooperation and improvements in domestic policies, we must effectively respond to climate change. This concludes the climate briefing for September 17, 2026.
